subject: Architecture
title: Vertical Forests: Skyscrapers With Trees
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Vertical Forests: Skyscrapers With Trees.

hook.text: Milan's Bosco Verticale has 900 trees growing on its balconies — a vertical forest 380 feet above the street.

buildup.text: Architect Stefano Boeri designed the towers to absorb CO2, produce oxygen, and reduce urban heat.

discovery.text: The trees filter 30 tons of CO2 per year and produce 19 tons of oxygen — the equivalent of a small forest.

twist.text: Maintaining trees 30 stories up requires 'flying gardeners' — arborists who rappel down the building facade.

climax.text: Boeri is designing forest cities in China — entire urban districts covered in vegetation from ground to roof.

punchline.text: Cities cut down forests to grow. Now they're growing forests on buildings.

quiz.question: How are the trees on Bosco Verticale maintained?
options: Automated irrigation systems handle all tree care
Arborists rappel down the facade to tend the trees
Residents on each floor maintain their own balcony trees

details.summary: Vertical forests are residential towers with trees and shrubs planted on every balcony, creating a living green facade. Stefano Boeri's Bosco Verticale in Milan was the prototype, hosting 900 trees that absorb CO2, produce oxygen, moderate temperatures, and support biodiversity in the city center.
details.whyItMatters: Vertical forests bring nature into dense urban environments where horizontal green space is scarce. They demonstrate that architecture can actively support biodiversity and air quality rather than merely reducing its own negative impact.
takeaways: The Bosco Verticale in Milan hosts 900 trees on its balconies
Trees absorb CO2, produce oxygen, and moderate temperatures
The concept brings biodiversity into dense urban centers

faq.question: Do the trees on vertical forest buildings survive?
faq.answer: Yes, with specialized care. Trees are selected for wind resistance and local climate. Automated irrigation systems water each plant individually. Arborists perform regular maintenance by rappelling down the facade. Milan's Bosco Verticale trees have thrived since completion in 2014.

faq.question: Are vertical forests being built elsewhere?
faq.answer: Boeri's studio has designed vertical forests in Nanjing, Lausanne, Tirana, Cairo, and other cities. The concept has inspired similar projects worldwide. Each adapts to local climate with regionally appropriate tree species, proving the concept is transferable across geographies.
